In this case, we have to use the identity

$$
1+{cot}^{2}⁡x={csc}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\frac{{cot}^{2}⁡x-1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x(1-{cot}^{4}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\frac{{cot}^{2}⁡x-1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x(1-{cot}^{2}⁡x)(1+{cot}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\frac{1-{cot}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x(1-{cot}^{2}⁡x)(1+{cot}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x(1+{cot}^{2}⁡x)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x{csc}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\int }_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /3}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =0-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
